critical.issue: Seed is NOT idempotent to app_id. The six canonical seeded tenants documented in /app/memory/test_credentials.md (app_6663b5de0007 Northwind Roofing, app_e3cb4f084785 Studio Booking, app_abc693a75574 Aura Wellness, app_1cb6f2b89eb6 Nexus Commerce, app_c18671970769 Design V2 Demo, app_b61ee44668e4 Plugin Restore Test) are all missing. A new seed run generated 6 fresh tenants with random ids, breaking every regression suite that hardcoded the old ids and severing the client.editor member relationship. Seed should upsert deterministically by app_id or by name so re-seeding preserves the known tenants (and their membership rows).

rca of the issue: Root cause: seed_demo_apps in /app/backend/server.py (or wherever the demo-tenant seed lives) is non-idempotent by app_id. When the previous testing cleanup pass (referenced in test_credentials.md) removed the six canonical tenants, the next startup re-seeded SIX replacement tenants using freshly-generated app_ids and freshly-generated names, instead of restoring the documented canonical ids/names. Memberships (client.editor → app_6663b5de0007) are keyed on the old app_id and were not re-created against the new tenants. This cascaded into 53 test failures whose fixtures hardcode the canonical app_ids, and into a user-visible regression where the client-editor login shows an empty dashboard. Mitigation: make the seed function upsert deterministically ({app_id: <canonical>} match) with stable name+description defaults, and always ensure client.editor membership on app_6663b5de0007 is present after seed. As a defensive measure, add a startup consistency check that logs a WARNING when a tenant listed in test_credentials.md is absent.
